narrative.overview: The whole product is one cozy building seen in cross-section, like the cutaway pages of a children's picture book. You read status from the building itself: glowing windows mean a team is working, a coral balloon means someone is waiting for you. Step inside a floor and its front wall swings open like a dollhouse, revealing toon-shaded animal villagers at their desks.
keyCharacteristics: 3D world first; UI panels float above it on the left, right and bottom edges.
Toon shading (3-step ramp) with warm-brown ink outlines on villagers and trees.
Candy-pastel floors (mint, butter, peach, lilac, sky) on a white trim frame.
Rounded everything: RoundedBox furniture, pill chips, 14–26px UI radii.
Korean copy in a playful office-life voice.

rules.name: The Coral Means You Rule
rules.body: Coral appears only when 대표 has to decide something. Never use it for decoration or errors that need no action.

rules.name: The Status Lives in the Building Rule
rules.body: Working floors glow (window glass #ffe7a3 at 62%), idle floors stay sky glass (#cfefff at 42%). Don't add separate stat cards for what the building already shows.

dos: Do use the stroke icons from web/icons.js (24 grid, 2.2–2.4 stroke, round caps) for tool kinds and actions.
Do keep villagers toon-shaded with ink outlines and blush, built from rounded primitives.
Do give every new floor the next pastel in the theme rotation.
donts: Don't use emoji as icons in chips, journal or buttons; emoji are fine only inside a villager's spoken line.
Don't reuse characters, art or UI from existing games; the cozy tone is pinned, the art is ours.
Don't use coral for anything that doesn't need 대표's decision.
